name: Toiletries Packing List
description: Everything that goes in the wash bag, sorted by what fits a carry-on and what the hotel supplies anyway.

sections.title: Liquids (100 ml / 3.4 oz each, one clear bag)

items.text: Shampoo and conditioner, decanted into travel bottles
Shower gel or a solid soap bar
items.note: A solid bar is not a liquid, so it does not count against the bag.

items.text: Deodorant — stick and roll-on are exempt, spray is not

items.note: Usually allowed above 100 ml as a medical liquid, but declare it at the checkpoint.
Safety and disposable razors are fine in a carry-on; straight razors are not.

items.text: Prescription medicine in the original labelled packaging
Any medicine you take occasionally but would struggle to buy abroad
items.note: Names and strengths differ between countries, and some over-the-counter drugs at home are prescription-only elsewhere.

items.text: Contact lenses and a spare pair of glasses
Make-up, cut back to one look

items.note: Not supplied by most hostels, campsites or short-term rentals.

items.text: Clear quart-sized bag for the liquids
Seal each liquid in a small zip bag against pressure leaks
A laundry bag for what comes back dirty

faq.q: What is the carry-on liquid limit?
faq.a: Each container must hold 100 ml (3.4 oz) or less, and all of them together must fit in one clear resealable bag of about one quart or litre. The limit is the printed size of the container, so a half-empty 200 ml bottle is still refused.

faq.q: Do solid toiletries count as liquids?
faq.a: No. Soap bars, shampoo bars, solid deodorant sticks and toothpaste tablets fall outside the liquid rule entirely, which is the simplest way to free up space in the clear bag.

faq.q: Can I take medication over 100 ml in hand luggage?
faq.a: Prescription and essential medical liquids are generally allowed above the limit, including contact lens solution and baby milk. Carry them separately, declare them at the checkpoint, and keep the original labelled packaging.

Mid-range and upmarket hotels almost always supply soap, shampoo, body lotion and a hairdryer. Hostels, campsites and short-term rentals often supply none of it and may not provide towels either, so check the listing before deciding what to leave behind.
